correctness.rationale: PASS: The symmetric three-edge subdivision of each rose petal meets the unordered two-particle discrete cubical configuration criterion. Cell counts c0=m(2m+1), c1=3m(2m−1), c2=5*C(m,2) follow from explicit disjoint graph-cell pairs. Radial/peripheral squares have unique active free edges and then peripheral/peripheral squares admit free edges; all 2-cells collapse and the remaining graph is connected, with β1=1+3*C(m,2), proving the integral wedge-of-circles type. For each signed petal permutation, oriented fixed 0,1,2 cells give signed Lefschetz trace 1+(3a²+2ab−b²−3a−3b)/2−r on rational H1, including transposition square-coordinate sign; group averaging gives invariant dimensions 2 for S_m and 0 for B_m. An independently built cubical-cell complex exhaustively checked all B_m actions for m=2,3,4,5, valid collapses, connected residual graphs and character/invariants; the proof of arbitrary m is symbolic rather than finite extrapolation.
